title: Tablèt pistach (Haitian peanut brittle)
instructions: Add water, sugar, vanilla extract, ginger, cinnamon, nutmeg, salt, and anise star extract to a large nonstick saucepan and bring to a boil.
Add the peanuts and boil for 10-15 min or until mixture has thickened.
Remove the pan from the heat and continue to stir until the liquid has evaporated and the mixture is sticky.
Spoon peanut mixture into large cookie sized pieces on parchment paper or a nonstick baking mat and cool until hardened.
Store cooled brittle in an airtight tight container.
story: This a recipe my sister’s and I would make with our Grandmother. Every school year she would travel from Haiti to Connecticut and brave the New England winters to help care for us. When our school hosted multicultural nights, she would make tablèt pistach (peanut brittle) and tablèt kokoye (coconut brittle) with us to share our Haitian heritage. They were always a huge hit. Tablèt pistach is a popular street food in Haiti and is nostalgic of the sugar boom when sugar cane was a major cash crop produced in Haiti.
